questions.stem: How is Entitlement characterised in contrast to Authorisation?
options: Entitlement is granted only after an audit
Entitlement is something a manager must approve each time
Entitlement expires after every action
Entitlement is something you inherit, get by default, or get along with something else
Entitlement applies only to data, never to people
questions.explanation: Entitlement is something you inherit, that comes as a default, or that you get along with something else, whereas Authorisation comes because of an action.

questions.stem: Where does Authorisation come from, as distinct from Entitlement?
options: It comes because of an action, or it expects an action in the future
It comes automatically with a job title
It is inherited from a previous role
It is a default setting in every system
It is granted by the data itself
questions.explanation: Authorisation comes because of an action, or it expects an action in the future, which is why it has a prescriptive behaviour.

options: How things currently are
How things were in the past
How it should be, with an action expected
How a doctor records a diagnosis
How data is described in a catalogue
questions.explanation: Prescriptive means how it should be, and an action is expected.

options: How an action must be carried out
How a rule will be enforced
How a future decision will be made
How a manager approves a request
How it is
questions.explanation: Descriptive simply means how it is, which is why Entitlement, something you already have, is descriptive.

questions.stem: Which of the following has a Prescriptive behaviour?
options: Entitlement
Authorisation
Both Entitlement and Authorisation
Neither Entitlement nor Authorisation
Only Entitlement to leave
questions.explanation: The key phrase is that Authorisation has a Prescriptive behaviour whereas Entitlement has a Descriptive behaviour.

questions.stem: An employee is entitled to 20 annual leaves, and the manager can accept or reject a leave application. Which part of this example illustrates Authorisation?
options: The 20 annual leaves the employee has
The 12 medical leaves the employee has
The employee's job title
The manager's power to accept or reject the application
The leave policy document
questions.explanation: The leaves themselves are an Entitlement; the manager's authority to accept or reject the leave application is Authorisation.

questions.stem: A Procurement user who deals only with electronics can see only the electronics rows of a table that also holds furniture and IT hardware data. What does this illustrate?
options: Entitlement at the row level
Authorisation to delete data
Authentication of the user
Data Enrichment
A prescriptive action
questions.explanation: Being able to see only the electronics rows is an Entitlement that comes with the user's role, in this case applied at the row level.

questions.stem: In the Procurement example, a few people are able to fix or delete data in procurement tables to maintain data quality. What do they have?
options: Entitlement to see the tables
Descriptive behaviour
A default inheritance
Data Literacy
Authority to fix or delete data
questions.explanation: Seeing procurement tables is an Entitlement of the department, but the few people who may fix or delete data have Authorisation for that action.

questions.stem: A Vice President has a company car. How does the Entitlement versus Authorisation distinction apply?
options: The VP is authorised to own the car but entitled to sell it
The VP is entitled to the car only after driving it
The VP is entitled to have the car and authorised to use it for company use only
The VP is entitled to use the car for personal trips
The VP has neither entitlement nor authorisation
questions.explanation: The VP is Entitled to have a company car and at the same time Authorised to use it for company use only.

questions.stem: Can the terms Entitlement and Authorisation be used interchangeably?
options: Yes, they always mean the same thing
In a few places they can be, but mostly they should not be
No, never under any circumstances
Only when talking about leave policies
Only in database security
questions.explanation: There are a few places where both can be used interchangeably, but mostly they should not be; mixing them up is not 100% accurate.
